mentions.context: And yet Albert’s emphasis, in Chapter 13 for instance, on self-understanding of the intellect as the only activity which connects the intellect, while being in the body, to the intelligible realm, is not found in Pico.47 Theses 7–10 focus on sense perception. In thesis 7 we find that sound, accord- ing to its real existence, is brought to the beginning of the nerve responsible for hearing.48 This thesis in, of course, related to thesis 9 which is again about sound and hearing, but strangely enough, Pico placed between these two a the-

Pico and Albert the Great 201 it moves the audible nerve.54 Thus, Pico in both theses dedicated to the sense of hearing – theses 7 and 9 – accurately reflects Albert’s views, although he uses a slightly different terminology. Thesis 8 states that light in a medium has only intentional existence.55 Albert discusses the nature of light and sight, col- our, medium and intention, in his commentary on De anima, Book 2, Tract. 3,
